issues.description: The problem statement explicitly asks for a modifiable List<Meal> attribute named 'orders' (e.g., "a modifiable List<Meal> attribute called orders" and UML noting orders as a List), but the provided solution (and the surrounding template code style) implements orders as a Meal[] array. This mismatch between the specified type (List) and the actual/expected implementation (array) will confuse students about which collection type to use and may lead to incompatible implementations or failing tests if the autograder expects one or the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement and the starter/solution code consistent. Either: (A) change the problem text to request an array-based orders field (Meal[] orders) to match the template/solution and helper utilities, or (B) change the solution/template to use a modifiable List<Meal> (and update ArrayHelpers/usages accordingly). Preferably align the statement with the existing array-based codebase (or update all template helpers to use List) to avoid mixed collection types.

issues.description: The problem statement contains a contradictory description of the 'stock' attribute: one place instructs students to create a final Stock stock initialized in the constructor (implying an instance final field set at construction), while a later note states that the 'stock' attribute must be static (shared across all instances). These are incompatible instructions and will confuse students whether to declare stock as an instance final field or a static (class-level) field.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: explicitly state whether 'stock' should be an instance final field (initialized in the constructor) or a class-level static field. Update the UML and textual description to match. If the intention is for a shared stock across all saloons, specify 'private static final Stock stock' and instruct students to initialize it as a static field (not in the instance constructor). If the intention is per-instance stock, remove the 'must be static' requirement and keep 'final Stock stock' initialized in the constructor.
